name: Washed Process
description: Beans are fermented in water to remove the cherry and mucilage, then dried. This method produces a cleaner, more acidic cup with brighter flavors.

name: Natural Process
description: Whole beans are dried in the sun with the cherry fruit intact. This method produces fruity, full-bodied coffees with lower acidity.

name: Semi-Washed Process
description: Also called pulped natural, beans are pulped but dried with some mucilage remaining. This method balances characteristics of washed and natural processes.

name: Anaerobic Fermentation
description: Beans are fermented in an oxygen-free environment, producing complex, wine-like flavors with intense aromatics.

name: Honey Process
description: A hybrid method where some mucilage is left on the bean during drying, creating sweet, balanced coffees.
